lessons.title: Receivables Work Areas and the Transaction Lifecycle

slots.practicalActivity: In your Oracle Fusion practice environment, open the Receivables work area and click through its sub-areas (Billing, Receipts, Collections) without entering anything yet. On paper, sketch the full order-to-cash chain -- order to shipment to invoice to receipt to cash application -- and mark exactly where Receivables' own responsibility begins and ends, mirroring the procure-to-pay diagram from the Payables course.
slots.deliverable: A written tour of the Receivables work area's sub-areas, plus a hand-drawn order-to-cash diagram marking Receivables' scope.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup and Maintenance, locate Manage Receivables System Options for your business unit and record its AutoAccounting rule set and cash/tax account defaults exactly as configured. Then open Manage Receivables Payment Terms, inspect an existing term, and build a new one named "2% 10 Net 30" offering a 2% discount within 10 days, otherwise due in 30 -- using the Lesson 5 self-check ("a customer should get 2% off if they pay within 10 days") as your test case.
slots.deliverable: A written record of your BU's real Receivables system options, plus a newly created "2% 10 Net 30" payment term saved in the practice environment.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Receivables Fundamentals: using the Lesson 3 setup map (system options, payment terms, trading community/customers, transaction types, sources, activities, memo lines, AutoAccounting), write a one-line diagnosis naming the exact setup object responsible for each of these four symptoms: (1) a customer should get 2% off for paying within 10 days, (2) every invoice to a certain customer should default to a specific GL account, (3) a write-off needs a bad-debt expense account, (4) a recurring $500 service charge needs a reusable description. Verify each against the real task names in Setup and Maintenance.
slots.deliverable: A four-symptom diagnostic worksheet matching each problem to its correct Receivables setup object, verified against real Setup and Maintenance task names.

lessons.title: The Trading Community Model: Parties, Accounts and Sites

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment's Customers work area, recreate the Lesson 7 Cascade Outdoor Supply example: search the party registry first to confirm no match exists, create a new organization party "Cascade Outdoor Supply," add a warehouse address as a party site, create a customer account "Cascade Outdoor Supply - US" with the standard profile class, and create one account site from that address carrying both Bill-To and Ship-To uses.
slots.deliverable: A real customer record "Cascade Outdoor Supply" created in the practice environment with one account site carrying Bill-To and Ship-To uses.

slots.practicalActivity: Continuing the Cascade Outdoor Supply record, add a named billing contact (an AP contact for invoice questions, as the lesson describes) and a second account site for a separate shipping location. Then override the account's credit limit away from its inherited profile-class default, setting a specific dollar ceiling, and write down what you'd expect to happen the next time a transaction would push Cascade over that limit.
slots.deliverable: The Cascade Outdoor Supply record updated with a billing contact, a second account site, and a manually overridden credit limit.

slots.practicalActivity: Attach a customer bank account to Cascade Outdoor Supply for automatic receipt processing, using an account number you invent for practice purposes only. Then create a second, deliberately near-duplicate customer record ("Cascade Outdoor Supply Inc.") and use the customer merge task to combine it into the original, confirming only one active record remains.
slots.deliverable: A bank account attached to Cascade Outdoor Supply, plus a completed customer-merge exercise leaving one clean active record.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Customers: build one complete, billable customer record from scratch in the practice environment, end to end -- party search, organization party, address, customer account with profile class, an account site with Bill-To and Ship-To uses, a contact, and a bank account -- without reusing Cascade Outdoor Supply. Document each step the way the Northwind Fixtures Co. worked example in Lesson 7 was described, to prove the record is actually invoice-ready.
slots.deliverable: A brand-new, fully invoice-ready customer record built independently in the practice environment, documented step by step.

slots.practicalActivity: In Setup and Maintenance, review an existing Invoice transaction type and record its natural sign and default accounting behavior. Then create a new manual transaction batch source named "Practice Manual Invoices" and, separately, examine how an "OM AutoInvoice Import" style source (as described in Lesson 21's worked example) would be configured differently for numbering and defaulting.
slots.deliverable: A written record of an Invoice transaction type's behavior, plus a newly created manual batch source compared against an import-style source.

slots.practicalActivity: Recreate the Lesson 14 Northwind Fixtures Co. example in the practice environment: create an "AR Adjustments - Bad Debt" Adjustment-type receivables activity pointing to a bad-debt expense account, and an "Early Payment Discount" Earned Discount activity pointing to a contra-revenue account. Then build a reusable memo line named "Service Charge - Rush Order" with its own default GL account, ready to use on a future debit memo.
slots.deliverable: Two new receivables activities (Adjustment and Earned Discount) and one new memo line, all created and saved in the practice environment.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short memo explaining, in your own words, the difference between recognizing revenue immediately at invoice time versus recognizing it over a schedule (for example a service contract billed up front but earned over 12 months), and why Receivables needs a revenue scheduling rule to handle the second case correctly. Locate the revenue scheduling rule setup screen in Setup and Maintenance and record what fields it requires.
slots.deliverable: A written explanation of immediate versus scheduled revenue recognition, plus a record of the real revenue scheduling rule setup fields.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Transaction Setup: write a short readiness checklist confirming every object this chapter covered is now in place in your practice environment before Chapter 4's hands-on invoicing begins -- one transaction type, one batch source, one receivables activity, one memo line, and an understanding of which transactions in your practice business unit would need a revenue scheduling rule versus immediate recognition.
slots.deliverable: A completed five-item transaction-setup readiness checklist confirmed against your own practice environment configuration.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment, create a manually entered invoice against the customer record you built in the Customers lab, using the manual batch source from the previous chapter, with two product lines, a freight line, and tax calculated automatically. Confirm the invoice total reconciles to the sum of its lines, tax, and freight before moving on.
slots.deliverable: One manually entered Receivables invoice with product, freight, and tax lines, reconciled to its header total.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the memo line built earlier, enter a debit memo billing a rush-order service charge back to your practice customer. Then enter a chargeback against the invoice from the previous slot (treating part of it as disputed and reopened as a new debit balance), and separately issue a full credit memo against a different invoice, writing down the natural-sign difference between a debit memo and a credit memo.
slots.deliverable: One debit memo (using the practice memo line), one chargeback, and one credit memo, all entered in the practice environment with a written sign-convention comparison.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a process memo recreating the Lesson 21 Northwind Fixtures Co. example in your own words: 400 staged lines, validation, grouping, and transfer, including what happens to the 3 lines that fail because of an end-dated customer site. Then complete and print (or preview) one of your own practice invoices, confirming its status moves from Incomplete to Complete before it becomes available for printing.
slots.deliverable: A written AutoInvoice three-phase process memo with its error-handling path, plus one practice transaction completed and printed/previewed.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Transactions: in the practice environment, run one customer through four transaction types in a single sitting -- a standard invoice with tax and freight, a debit memo, a chargeback, and a credit memo -- and complete each one. Write a short summary table showing each transaction's natural sign and net effect on the customer's open balance.
slots.deliverable: Four completed transaction types (invoice, debit memo, chargeback, credit memo) for one customer, with a summary table of sign and balance effect.

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment, enter a standard receipt for the exact amount of one of your completed invoices and apply it in full. Then enter a miscellaneous receipt representing an interest payment or rebate that isn't tied to any invoice, posting it directly to the Miscellaneous Cash receivables activity you'd expect to use for that kind of deposit.
slots.deliverable: One standard receipt fully applied to an invoice, plus one miscellaneous receipt posted against a non-invoice deposit.

slots.practicalActivity: Recreate the Lesson 25 Meridian Office Supply overpayment example: enter one receipt for $4,500 against an invoice open for $4,250, apply $4,250 to close it, and leave $250 unapplied on the same receipt. Then deliberately misapply a second receipt to the wrong invoice, unapply it, and reapply it correctly, confirming both the receipt's and the transaction's balances return to the right state after the fix.
slots.deliverable: One overpaid receipt with $250 correctly left unapplied, plus one misapplied-then-corrected receipt demonstrating unapply and reapply.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the customer bank account set up earlier, create an automatic receipt batch and remit it, noting how it differs from manually entering a standard receipt one at a time. Then write a process memo describing how a lockbox file from a bank would stage receipt data for import, and what happens to a record in that file that fails validation -- the mirror image of AutoInvoice's error-handling path from Chapter 4.
slots.deliverable: One automatic receipt batch created and remitted, plus a written lockbox-processing memo covering its validation-failure path.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick one applied receipt from earlier in this chapter and reverse it in the practice environment, as if the customer's check bounced. Confirm the originally closed invoice reopens with its balance due restored, and write a one-paragraph note on how this differs from simply unapplying a receipt that was matched to the wrong invoice.
slots.deliverable: One reversed receipt with its underlying invoice reopened, plus a written comparison of reversal versus unapply.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Receipts: run one customer through the full receipt lifecycle in a single sitting -- a standard receipt applied in full, an overpayment left partially unapplied, a misapplied-and-corrected receipt, and one reversed receipt -- and write a short cash-application log summarizing each receipt's final disposition.
slots.deliverable: A four-scenario receipt lifecycle (full application, overpayment, correction, reversal) for one customer, with a written cash-application log.

slots.practicalActivity: Recreate the Lesson 14/30 Northwind pattern: adjust off a small $25 rounding difference on a closed invoice using your Adjustment-type receivables activity, confirming it posts automatically to bad-debt expense with no manual account entry. Then attempt a larger write-off that exceeds your own approval limit (check what limit is configured for your role) and write down what Receivables does when a write-off request is outside the requester's authority.
slots.deliverable: One small adjustment posted via the Adjustment activity, plus a documented over-limit write-off attempt showing the approval-limit control.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Collections Workbench for your practice customer and review its aging buckets and dunning history. Configure aged dunning on the customer's account and generate a first-level dunning letter for a past-due invoice, then separately print a customer statement and run an aging report, confirming all three tools agree on which balances are actually overdue.
slots.deliverable: One dunning letter generated through the Collections Workbench, plus a printed customer statement and an aging report, cross-checked for agreement.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick three of your practice transactions from earlier chapters (one invoice, one credit memo, one receipt) and run Create Accounting in Draft mode to preview the journal entries, then re-run it in Final mode. Record each transaction's resulting accounted status and write down, in your own words, what final accounting locks in that draft mode does not.
slots.deliverable: A written log of three practice transactions run through Create Accounting in Draft and Final mode, with resulting accounted statuses.

slots.practicalActivity: Transfer the Final-mode journal batches from the previous slot to the General Ledger and confirm they post. Then work the full Lesson 38 close sequence against your practice business unit for the current period -- finish month-end activity, run final accounting, set the period to Close Pending, run the Prepare Receivables to General Ledger Reconciliation process, and review the resulting Receivables to Ledger Reconciliation Report to see whether it ties. Finish by working all three Lesson 39 diagnostic scenarios in writing (the Meridian Office Supply unapplied-receipt false alarm, the $4,250 GL-versus-Receivables reconciliation gap, and the Brightline Retail Group dispute-versus-collectible-balance decision), naming the specific chapter and tool that resolves each, then write a two-paragraph course capstone naming the single biggest mistake a brand-new AR clerk would make in their first month and exactly which lesson prevents it.
slots.deliverable: A posted GL batch traced through transfer and post, a completed period-close sequence through Close Pending with a reviewed reconciliation report, written diagnoses for all three course-closing troubleshooting scenarios, and a capstone summary naming the biggest new-AR-clerk mistake and its preventive lesson.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can run the full Oracle Fusion Receivables cycle hands-on in the practice environment -- creating and maintaining customers, entering invoices, debit memos, chargebacks and credit memos, applying and reversing receipts, managing adjustments, write-offs and collections, and closing and reconciling a Receivables period against the General Ledger.
